title: TEMPO: Prompt-Based Generative Pre-Trained Transformer for Time Series Forecasting
authors: Cao, D.; Jia, F.; Arik, S.O.; Pfister, T.; Zheng, Y.; Ye, W.; Liu, Y.
tldr: TEMPO decomposes time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components and feeds them with learned prompts into a GPT-2 backbone, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot forecasting across seven benchmark datasets.
problem_and_motivation: Deep learning architectures for time series forecasting vary widely across domains and require per-task training from scratch, limiting generalization.
approach: Decompose each input channel into trend, seasonal, and residual components via STL.
Learnable parameters align local decomposition with global STL decomposition through MSE loss.
Apply reverse instance normalization to each component separately.
Patch time series into tokens and embed each component into GPT-2 input space.
Design component-specific semi-soft prompts using semantic initialization.
Feed concatenated prompt-plus-component embeddings through 6-layer GPT-2 decoder with LoRA adaptation.
Split GPT-2 output into component-specific predictions and sum them for final forecast.
Construct interpretable GAM on GPT-2 output to quantify component contributions via SHAP values.
Evaluate under zero-shot many-to-one setting across diverse source and target domains.
findings: num: TEMPO improves MAE by 6.5% over PatchTST on weather benchmark dataset.
num: TEMPO improves MAE by 19.1% over PatchTST on ETTm1 benchmark dataset.
num: Removing prompt component reduces average MSE and MAE across all benchmarks.
num: SHAP analysis reveals seasonal component has dominant influence on predictions for strongly periodic datasets.
num: TEMPO zero-shot performance surpasses full-shot state-of-the-art models on ETTh1 and ETTh2.
num: Semi-soft and hard prompts outperform purely soft random-init prompts.
num: Pre-trained language model baselines outperform transformer-from-scratch models in zero-shot cross-domain forecasting.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: TEMPO introduces a prompt-based generative transformer architecture for time series forecasting that adapts pre-trained language models through STL decomposition and learned soft prompts. Demonstrates that decomposing time series into trend, seasonal, and residual components before feeding to GPT-2 yields significant zero-shot forecasting gains.
directly_justifies: Time series decomposition into trend, seasonal, and residual components is essential because self-attention cannot disentangle non-orthogonal signals.
TEMPO improves MAE by 6.5% and 19.1% over PatchTST on weather and ETTm1 benchmarks.
Zero-shot TEMPO performance surpasses full-shot state-of-the-art models on ETTh1 and ETTh2.
Semi-soft prompts with semantic initialization outperform purely soft random-initialized prompts.
limits: Paper acknowledges superior LLMs with better numerical reasoning might yield better results.
Experiments limited to GPT-2 backbone; larger models not explored.
Zero-shot evaluation relies on specific many-to-one training protocol.

limitations: Paper acknowledges superior LLMs with better numerical reasoning might yield better results.
Larger backbone models beyond GPT-2 6-layer were not explored.
Zero-shot many-to-one training protocol assumes equal sampling from source domains.
Prompt pool design is noted as initial exploration with substantial room for advancing.
